inputs.share_count_basis: 1,000,000,000 ordinary shares at 30-Jun-2026 (AR26 note 25.3; no options, no LTI, no convertibles). Held FLAT; SBC is nil so there is nothing to expense or dilute.

net_debt_bridge.note: Bluecurrent (carrying value $580.4m = 50% share of net assets 399.2 + shareholder loans 179.6 + FX 1.6) is EXCLUDED from adjusted EBITDA, so it enters the bridge at value (matching-asset rule, owner-fcf.md 7d). Valued at $700m = FY26 cash distributions to Vector of $55m (dividend 32.6 + loan interest 10.2 + loan repayment 12.1) capitalised at a 10% cost of equity with 2% growth; that is 1.2x carrying value and a 7.9% cash yield. Every +/-$100m on this line is +/-$0.10/share. The $35.3m prepaid tax asset will be consumed against FY27 cash tax, so the model runs a full 28% cash tax rate from FY27 and credits the asset here instead. Derivatives (net asset $11.4m) hedge the USPP face value already counted and are left out.

inputs.sbc_source: AR26 remuneration report: STI only, no LTI plan; only an employee share purchase scheme reserve (immaterial). SBC treated as zero.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY26 interest received $14.7m ($10.2m of it Bluecurrent shareholder-loan interest). NOT in the FCF base: adjusted EBITDA excludes all interest; the Bluecurrent loan is valued inside the $700m JV line and cash is netted in economic net debt.

guidance_fy27.note: FY27 adj EBITDA includes ~$54m of one-off revenue wash-up + IRIS adjustments (management, 18-Aug-2026). Modelled as FY27 revenue +9% then FY28 -1% as the wash-up drops out.

inputs.wacc_rationale: NZD-built: NZ 10y govt ~4.4% + beta 0.65 x ERP 5.5% = 8.0% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.3% (FY26 blended 4.6% on face debt, marginal higher) -> 3.8% post-tax; weights at market (equity $4.72bn / economic net debt $2.28bn = 32.6% debt) -> 6.6%, rounded to 6.75%. Same WACC in all three scenarios (risk lives in the driver paths, owner-fcf.md 7f). For reference the Commerce Commission's DPP4 allowed WACC is ~7%; a DCF discounted at the regulated WACC returns ~1.0x RAB by construction.
notes: MODEL: component owner-FCF DCF (owner-fcf.md) with regulated-network adaptations; the dcf-methods routing table has no dedicated regulated-utility row, and the closest match (non-US operating company + section 7) is used with the RAB identity as the sanity cross-check. Not an AFFO/REIT model (Vector is an operating utility with EBITDA, not a fair-value property trust) and not a book-value model (NTA is not RAB).

REVENUE BASE = revenue excluding capital contributions ($1,004.4m FY26). CAPITAL CONTRIBUTIONS ($191.5m cash FY26) are netted against gross capex, mirroring Vector's own adjusted-EBITDA / net-capex framing. Reported EBITDA (673.1) and CSV EBITDA include contributions and must not be compared with adj EBITDA here.

CAPEX SUPERCYCLE: raw FCF is structurally negative/near zero because net capex (34% of revenue FY26, 41% FY27 guidance) exceeds D&A (23%). In a RAB regime that growth capex earns the regulated return, so revenue growth is tied to RAB growth (net capex - depreciation + CPI indexation, ~6-7%/yr nominal in DPP4) with an explicit DPP5 step in FY31 (base +9%, bull +12%, bear -5%). Terminal-year net capex is normalised to what 3% nominal growth needs (D&A 23.5% + ~1% real RAB growth = ~28% of revenue); leaving capex at the supercycle level while crediting only 3% growth is the classic way this ticker gets undervalued.

TAX: 28% NZ statutory on EBIT (adj EBITDA - D&A) in every year. FY26 cash tax paid was only $1.4m because a prepaid tax asset was being consumed; that asset ($35.3m remaining) is credited in the bridge rather than through a low first-year rate. Accelerated tax depreciation (deferred tax +$45m/yr) and the taxability of capital contributions (~$53m) roughly offset, so 28% on EBIT is within ~$10m of FY26's unlevered current tax.
LEASES: treatment (A) - lease liabilities ($52.3m) inside economic net debt; the ~$5.5m/yr lease cash cost is carried as +0.5pp inside the capex % path (no separate lease_cost_pct).
NCI: none since the Liquigas sale (equity 100% attributable). Bluecurrent is an equity-accounted JV, handled in the bridge.

HISTORY: FY2023 net income $1,715.8m is ~$1,510m metering disposal gain; FY24/FY25 carry $60.6m/$37.0m gas impairments; all pre-FY25 rows in the CSV include since-sold gas trading. Nothing before the FY26 continuing-operations base is extrapolated.

RAB CROSS-CHECK (estimate, not disclosed in the annual report): electricity RAB ~$4.2bn (Mar-2026) + gas ~$0.5bn = ~$4.7bn +/-10%. Market EV ex non-operating assets = $6.24bn = ~1.33x RAB, i.e. the market discounts Vector at ~6.0% or pays for outperformance/scarcity. Base-case network EV of ~$4.5bn is ~0.95x RAB, consistent with a 6.75% WACC against a ~7% regulated WACC less the value leakage from gas decline and DPP5 reset risk.

DIVIDEND: FY26 26.0cps ($255m) unimputed, 5.5% yield, ~3.5x the unlevered owner FCF - the payout is funded by the growing debt book while gearing (38.5%) has headroom to the ~45-50% band Vector ran pre-2023. Entrust's 75.1% holding makes the dividend politically sticky.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: regulatory building blocks: nominal RAB growth (net capex less regulatory depreciation, plus CPI indexation), decelerating to 3% terminal - not a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Every historical CAGR is distorted: revenue/EBITDA/EPS 'CAGRs' are continuing-operations series (AR26 five-year summary, FY22-FY26, so the '5yr' slots are 4-year figures) and are dominated by the April-2025 DPP4 reset (+20% adj EBITDA in one year); EPS bases carry the FY24/FY25 gas impairments; equity CAGRs are broken by the $1.5bn FY23 metering gain (5yr +9.2%, 3yr -2.9%); owner FCF changes sign (FY23 -25.8, FY25 +93.6) so its CAGR is undefined. None of them is a forward growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF history = adj EBITDA - 28% x adj EBIT - (gross capex - capital contributions), continuing ops; FY26 on the accrual capex basis (544 - 191) is 59.4 vs 72.6 on the cash basis used as last_fcf.
historical_growth.db_series_note: core_metrics Revenue/EPS include the metering (sold FY23) and gas trading (sold FY24-25) businesses, so the total-revenue CAGRs are negative (-6.3% 3yr, -1.3% 5yr) and describe divestment, not the network. The headline revenue/EBITDA/EPS CAGRs above are the AR26 five-year-summary continuing-operations series (FY22 902.9 -> FY26 1,195.3 incl. contributions; adj EBITDA 316.8 -> 482.2; NP continuing 137.3 -> 240.2); the '5yr' slots are four-year figures because the continuing series starts at FY22.

scenario_narratives.base: DPP4 (to Mar-2030) plays out as set: FY27 revenue +9% including the ~$54m wash-up/IRIS one-off that then drops out (FY28 -1%), CPI+RAB growth of ~5% a year thereafter. Net capex runs at the guided ~$450m in FY27 (41% of revenue) and tapers to 28% by FY36 as the replacement wave passes and data-centre/EV growth capex normalises. DPP5 (Apr-2030) resets on a RAB ~25-30% larger at a similar ~7% WACC, giving a +9% revenue step in FY31. Adj EBITDA margin holds ~48.5% (opex inflation offset by scale). Gas distribution declines slowly inside the blend. WACC 6.75%, terminal growth 3% (CPI ~2% + ~1% real RAB growth).
scenario_narratives.bull: Auckland electrification and the flagged 500MW of data-centre load arrive on schedule, the capex programme is delivered efficiently (IRIS rewards rather than penalties), the DPP5 reset lands with a high allowed WACC (rates stay ~4-4.5%) on the enlarged RAB (+12% FY31 step), and the new CEO's efficiency review lifts the margin to 50%. Capex intensity falls faster (27% by FY36) as demand-side orchestration (Symphony) defers reinforcement. Terminal growth 3.25%.
scenario_narratives.bear: NZ rates fall back toward 2021 levels before the DPP5 reset, so the allowed return on the larger RAB is cut (FY31 -5% revenue step) while political pressure on Auckland lines charges tightens the path; capex over-runs and IRIS penalties leave part of the record capex programme unrecognised (capex stays 30%+ of revenue), opex inflation and storm/resilience costs compress the margin to 46%, gas distribution volumes decline faster than accelerated depreciation recovers. Terminal growth 2.5%.

entry_price.method: 15% IRR: PV of interim owner FCF at 15% + terminal value BUILT at 15% (min(Gordon@15%, 30x FCF_N)) discounted 10 years, less bridge net debt, per share; per scenario then probability-weighted.
entry_price.entry_price_note: NO positive price meets a 15% hurdle in any scenario: at 15% the PV of ten years of thin supercycle FCF plus a terminal value built at 15% is below the $1.52bn bridge net debt, so the unfloored entry prices are negative. entry_price is floored at 0.00 and the unfloored figure retained. A regulated network geared ~35% cannot return 15% to equity from its allowed ~7% return; the required_return_table is the useful reading (9% -> $0.83, 6.75% -> base IV $2.59).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (min(Gordon@r, 30x FCF_N)). 6.75% row = valuation.base.intrinsic_value; 15% row = entry_price.base.entry_price_unfloored. Market price NZ$4.72 exceeds the 6.75% row; it is reached only at a discount rate of roughly 6.0%.

sensitivity.note: WACC +/-1pp (not +/-2pp: a 4.75% nominal WACC is below the regulated allowed return and meaningless), terminal growth +/-1pp. Cells where the 30x cap binds are reported at the cap.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 house default. Bear raised to 25%: essentially all earnings depend on one regulator's five-yearly reset and the next one (DPP5, Apr-2030) falls inside the explicit horizon; gas distribution is a slowly stranding asset; the dividend is debt-funded through a record capex programme. Bull cut to 25%: it needs rates to stay high into the DPP5 reset AND the data-centre load AND efficient delivery of $600m+/yr capex, three independent things.
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC is nil, so house and street bases coincide and the band collapses to a point; band_position is n/a rather than a degenerate 0%.

market_context.rab_estimate_note: RAB ~NZ$4.7bn (electricity ~4.2bn at Mar-2026 + gas ~0.5bn) is an analyst estimate from Vector's information disclosures trend and DPP4 building blocks; the FY26 annual report does not print it. Treat as +/-10%.
market_context.price_implied_discount_rate_note: The required-return table puts the NZ$4.72 price at an implied nominal WACC of roughly 6.0% on the base drivers, i.e. the market capitalises Vector at ~1.33x RAB. That premium is the scarcity/Entrust-control/inflation-hedge premium NZ regulated infrastructure has carried for a decade (compare AIA.NZ), not something the flows justify at a 6.75% WACC.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Regulated-network owner-FCF DCF: the value of a RAB business at the regulated WACC is the RAB, so the model's job is to price the gap between the market's ~6% implied rate and a 6.75% cost of capital, plus the specific leakages (gas decline, DPP5 reset, debt-funded dividend) that make Vector worth a little less than its RAB.
key_judgments: Revenue growth follows RAB growth, with the DPP5 reset made explicit in FY31 and terminal capex normalised to terminal growth
Capital contributions net against capex, never counted as revenue or EBITDA
Bluecurrent valued on cash distributions in the bridge because adjusted EBITDA excludes it
One WACC across scenarios; regulatory and stranding risk carried in the driver paths and the 25% bear weight
